newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk rebel MP says new govt not for elections.
newsitem.headline: Turk rebel MP says new govt not for elections.

text.p: A dissident Turkish government deputy said on Tuesday his planned alternative coalition excluding the ruling Islamists would aim to rule rather than hold fresh elections.

"This government will not be for elections it will be a solution government," former trade and industry minister Yalim Erez told reporters after talks with a leftist leader on setting up a new coalition.

Erez earlier met the leader of Turkey's main opposition party, who said the two agreed fully on a coalition formula that would shut out the Islamist Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan after 11 troubled months in power.

Disagreements among the major right-wing and leftist parties have thwarted previous attempts to establish a government not including Welfare. Such disagreements led to the formation of the existing coalition last June.
Erez and another deputy from the conservative True Path Party (DYP) resigned last month in protest at the Islamists' failure to back an army-inspired crackdown on religious activism.
The government has been deeply divided over the reluctance of Welfare to support reforms of the education system which it fears would erode the role of religious schools in Turkey.
